summary_en: As Magic: The Gathering's The Hobbit: Tales of Middle-earth set drops, we're diving into the cards that are already commanding top dollar, offering a glimpse into what collectors and players are chasing.

en.title: The 10 Most Valuable Cards in The Hobbit's MTG Set
en.summary: As Magic: The Gathering's The Hobbit: Tales of Middle-earth set drops, we're diving into the cards that are already commanding top dollar, offering a glimpse into what collectors and players are chasing.
en.body:
## 10. The Queen of Dale (Showcase) (Surge Foil)
This version of The Queen of Dale is currently fetching around $160 and introduces the intriguing 'Recruit' mechanic. This ability lets you draw and discard a card, creating a 1/1 white Human Soldier token if you discard a nonland card, allowing for rapid board development and graveyard synergy at a low mana cost.

## 9. Thranduil, the Elvenking (Borderless) (Surge Foil)
Sporting a striking book cover art treatment, Thranduil, the Elvenking is a 5/6 creature that grants access to all activated abilities of Elf cards in your graveyard. It also synergizes beautifully with other legendary Elves, drawing and discarding cards when another enters the battlefield, making it a powerhouse for Elf-typal strategies in green and blue.

## 8. Thorin, Mountain-king (Borderless) (Surge Foil)
Another card boasting book cover art, Thorin, Mountain-king, a Dwarf Noble, is central to The Hobbit's narrative. This card allows you to attach equipment to one of your creatures for free, significantly accelerating your strategy by enabling powerful equipment synergies without the usual mana investment.

## 7. Smaug, the Magnificent
While specific pricing details were not available for this particular entry in the source, Smaug, the Magnificent is noted as a significant chase card from the set. As the iconic dragon of The Hobbit, its presence in Magic: The Gathering is expected to drive high demand among collectors and players alike.

## 6. The Arkenstone
The Arkenstone is another high-value card that players are eager to pull from The Hobbit set. Its significance in the lore suggests a powerful in-game effect, making it a desirable centerpiece for many decks and a prime target for those looking to acquire the set's most potent treasures.

## 5. Gandalf, the White
Gandalf, the White, is positioned as one of the most sought-after cards from this crossover. As a central figure in Tolkien's legendarium, Gandalf's representation in Magic is anticipated to be both mechanically impactful and highly collectible, driving its price up.

## 4. Gandalf, Friend of the Shire
This iteration of Gandalf, focusing on his connection to the Shire, is also appearing on lists of the most valuable cards. Its specific abilities are likely to offer unique strategic advantages, making it a key card for players seeking to optimize their decks with thematic and powerful options.

## 3. Bilbo Baggins, Birthday Boy
Bilbo's iconic status as the protagonist of The Hobbit makes this card a must-have for many fans. The 'Birthday Boy' moniker suggests a card that celebrates a key moment, likely translating into strong gameplay mechanics that appeal to both collectors and competitive players.

## 2. Aragorn, King of Gondor
Representing a pivotal character from the broader Legendarium that The Hobbit is a part of, Aragorn's appearance is a major draw. As King of Gondor, his card is expected to carry significant weight, both in terms of lore and potential power on the battlefield.

## 1. The One Ring
Though currently unpriced, The One Ring is undoubtedly the most anticipated and potentially most valuable card in the entire set. Its unparalleled significance in Tolkien's works makes it the ultimate chase card, with collectors and players alike speculating on its immense value upon official pricing.
Bottom Line: From iconic characters to powerful mechanics, The Hobbit's MTG set is packed with cards that are already proving to be highly valuable to players and collectors.

content_raw: For all of the controversy around Magic: The Gathering’s Universes Beyond sets, we imagine a lot of people were very excited for a return to Middle-Earth when The Hobbit was announced. Now, ahead of launch, we’re still wondering where those Commander Decks are, but we can console ourselves with some absolutely awesome artwork and some really cool new cards. Before we cover the set’s priciest cards, a couple of caveats: First is that we’re going via TCGplayer pricing, and there’s no amount attached to the One Ring just yet. The second is that pre-release pricing is notoriously fickle, and it’s likely these prices will shift quickly. Still, if you’re opening packs on launch weekend, these are the cards you should be looking for. The Most Valuable Cards In The Hobbit’s Magic: The Gathering Set 10 - The Queen of Dale (Showcase) (Surge Foil) - $160 Kicking off our list, this version of The Queen of Dale is sitting at $160 and lets you recruit when your opponents cast noncreature spells. Recruit, you say? This mechanic allows you to draw and discard a card, creating a 1/1 white Human Soldier token if you discard a nonland card. You can swiftly ramp up your side of the board (and your graveyard) if you’re recruiting for every noncreature spell, especially at a cost of just two mana. 9 - Thranduil, the Elvenking (Borderless) (Surge Foil) - $170 Our first book cover treatment (expect plenty more), Thranduil, the Elvenking is a 5/6 that has all activated abilities of Elf cards in your graveyard. It also allows you to draw cards and discard a card when another legendary Elf enters, making it ideal for typal synergies — and green and blue have a ton of access to Elves. It’s around $170. 8 - Thorin, Mountain-king (Borderless) (Surge Foil) - $195 Another book cover, Thorin, Mountain-King is core to the story of The Hobbit, and this Dwarf Noble attaches equipment to one of your creatures for free. When one or more pieces of equipment become attached to that creature this way, that creature deals damage equal to its power to up to one target creature. It’s also a 3/4 body with Trample, and is selling for around $195. 7 - Smaug the Magnificent (Borderless) - $200 One of the most striking visuals in the set, Smaug the Magnificent’s borderless treatment is going for around $200. It doesn’t say it on this version of the card, but this card deals damage equal to the number of Treasures you control to any target, be that a creature or a player. And, at the beginning of your upkeep, you get a Treasure token, too. All of that, plus it’s a 4/3 with flying and haste. 6 - Smaug the Magnificent (Showcase) (Surge Foil) - $225 More Smaug, anyone? Functionally the same as the above, this version shows the fearsome dragon napping on a pile of gold and treasure. It’s selling for around $225 right now. 5 - Bilbo, Thief in the Night (Showcase) (Surge Foil) - $225 Ah, finally - our cunning burglar Hobbit.
